topic: Hilbert argues that Poincaré's (automorphic) functions are the right foundation for the theory of algebraic functions and sketches two alternative ways of proving their existence, the second via a mapping between the totality of Riemann surfaces of genus p and the totality of Poincaré circular-arc polygons.

triage.modern_statement: The note asks which author's proof this is, so it is about who gets credit for a method, not an open mathematical question. The method in question: to prove that every compact Riemann surface (algebraic curve) of genus p ≥ 2 can be uniformized by Fuchsian groups (Poincaré's automorphic functions), use the 'continuity method' (Kontinuitätsmethode) of Klein and Poincaré. One takes the space of Riemann surfaces of genus p (moduli space, 3p−3 complex dimensions) and the space of Fuchsian groups / Poincaré circular-arc fundamental polygons of genus p (6p−6 real dimensions), and shows that the natural map from polygons to surfaces is one-to-one, continuous and proper, so by invariance of domain it is onto. Hilbert wonders whether Ludwig Schlesinger's treatment of the existence proof is this method.
triage.answered_by: Only partly settled, and the identification rests on what my searches found plus standard history. (a) The attribution: Ludwig Schlesinger did write up the Klein–Poincaré continuity method. His 'Vorlesungen über lineare Differentialgleichungen' (1908) has a section headed 'Kontinuitätsmethode' (§§286–304), and he also wrote 'Automorphe Funktionen' (1924). This makes it plausible that the method Hilbert sketches is the one Schlesinger presented, but I found no source that addresses Hilbert's note directly. (b) The underlying existence problem: Koebe (1912) completed the continuity method rigorously, and the general uniformization theorem was proved by Koebe and Poincaré in 1907. This is the topic of Hilbert's 22nd problem (1900).

evidence.claim: Schlesinger's 'Vorlesungen über lineare Differentialgleichungen' has a section titled 'Kontinuitätsmethode' (§§286–304), so Schlesinger did present the continuity method.
Schlesinger wrote a monograph 'Automorphe Funktionen' (Göschens Lehrbücherei, 1924).
The continuity method assigns Fuchsian groups to the set of Riemann surfaces of a given genus. The method was only made rigorous about thirty years later, by Koebe in 1912.

Historical work from about 1882 to 1907 led from uniformizing algebraic Riemann surfaces by the continuity method to the general uniformization theorem. In his 1900 problems lecture, Hilbert praises Poincaré's work on algebraic Riemann surfaces and uniformization.

triage.why: The note is a question about attribution: Hilbert asks whether the continuity-method proof he sketches is Schlesinger's. Sources show that Schlesinger did present the Klein–Poincaré continuity method in his textbooks, so the answer is plausibly yes. However, I found no source that discusses this specific note, and my search budget ran out before I could check Schlesinger's earlier 'Handbuch' (1895–98). The mathematics behind the note, existence of Fuchsian uniformization via a map between moduli space and the space of polygons, was settled by Koebe and Brouwer around 1912. It is part of Hilbert's 22nd problem (uniformization), which has been solved. The Brouwer invariance-of-domain link and the 22nd-problem link are standard history but are not fully covered by the sources cited above. Teichmüller theory is the modern continuation of these ideas, but this specific question is closed.
